authorized_evidence.content:
Storage Rules

Internal, Confidential, and Restricted data must be stored in approved company systems. Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should not be stored in local folders unless there is a documented business need.

Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.

On-Call Severity Levels

| Severity | Definition | Initial Response Target |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| SEV-1 | Widespread production outage or data exposure risk | 15 minutes |
| SEV-2 | Major workflow unavailable for multiple customers | 30 minutes |
| SEV-3 | Degraded feature with workaround available | 4 business hours |
| SEV-4 | Low-impact defect or documentation issue | Next planning cycle |

The on-call engineer owns triage until an incident commander is assigned. The incident commander owns status updates, escalation, and post-incident review scheduling.

Local Storage

Customer data, restricted data, and regulated data should not be stored locally unless there is a documented business need and approved protection. Files should be stored in company-approved cloud storage with access controls.

Sharing Rules

Employees may share data only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Confidential and Restricted data must not be shared in public channels or with unapproved external recipients.

Sales materials may be shared externally only when marked as customer-approved or public-facing.

SLA Targets

| Customer Tier | Initial Response | Status Update Cadence | Target Resolution |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enterprise | 1 business hour | Every 4 business hours | 2 business days |
| Growth | 4 business hours | Every business day | 5 business days |
| Standard | 1 business day | Every 2 business days | 10 business days |

The SLA clock starts when the customer provides enough detail to identify the affected workspace, workflow, or integration. Requests with missing identifiers should receive a clarification response, not a resolution promise.

Escalation Paths

Employee relations concerns should be escalated to People Operations. Security access issues should be escalated to IT Support. Customer-impacting delivery risks should be escalated to the relevant department leader.

Approved Software

Employees should use company-approved software for messaging, file storage, source control, project tracking, and customer collaboration. Unapproved software that stores company data must not be used without IT review.

Refund Guardrails

Sales Representatives may recommend a service credit up to USD 1,000 for an Enterprise customer when Northstar missed a documented SLA and the customer experienced measurable workflow disruption. The credit must be approved by a Manager before it is communicated.

Refunds above USD 1,000, refunds tied to contract terms, and refunds requested as part of legal settlement discussions require Manager and Legal review. Support should not promise refunds, credits, free renewals, or roadmap commitments without approval.

Classification Levels

Northstar uses four data classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted.

Public data is approved for external sharing. Internal data is intended for Northstar employees. Confidential data includes customer business information, financial forecasts, non-public sales materials, and employee operational data. Restricted data includes secrets, credentials, regulated customer data, privileged security records, and sensitive HR case material.

raw_response.answer: For an Enterprise customer reporting suspected data exposure, the support escalation owner is a Manager, as escalation to a Manager is triggered by suspected data exposure. If the incident is classified as SEV-1, the engineering initial-response target is 15 minutes, as SEV-1 severity corresponds to widespread production outage or data exposure risk with a 15-minute initial response target.
